bank.keyText: The aldehyde is reduced first because aldehydes are more electrophilic and less sterically hindered than ketones
choiceTexts: The aldehyde is reduced first because aldehydes are more electrophilic and less sterically hindered than ketones
The ketone is reduced first, because the two alkyl groups on a ketone make its carbonyl carbon more electrophilic than an aldehyde carbon
The aldehyde is reduced first because its carbonyl carbon is the more sterically hindered of the two and binds borohydride more tightly
Neither is reduced; NaBH4 only reduces esters
Both are reduced equally; NaBH4 shows no selectivity

answer.text: The aldehyde is reduced first because aldehydes are more electrophilic and less sterically hindered than ketones
answer.line: With only one equivalent in the cold, NaBH4 goes to the faster carbonyl: the aldehyde, which is more positive and less crowded.

steps: Find both carbonyls: a ketone at C4 and an aldehyde at C1, the chain end.
Rank them. The aldehyde carbon has one carbon group and an H; the ketone carbon has two carbon groups, more donation and more crowding.
One equivalent at 0 C goes to the faster target. The aldehyde becomes CH2OH and the ketone survives: 5-hydroxypentan-2-one.

choices.text: The aldehyde is reduced first because aldehydes are more electrophilic and less sterically hindered than ketones
choices.note: More positive and more open: the aldehyde takes the hydride first.

choices.text: The ketone is reduced first, because the two alkyl groups on a ketone make its carbonyl carbon more electrophilic than an aldehyde carbon
choices.note: Alkyl groups donate electron density, so the ketone carbon is less positive. The order runs the other way.

choices.text: The aldehyde is reduced first because its carbonyl carbon is the more sterically hindered of the two and binds borohydride more tightly
choices.note: The aldehyde does react first. But it is the less hindered of the two, and that openness is part of why.

choices.text: Neither is reduced; NaBH4 only reduces esters
choices.note: NaBH4 reduces aldehydes and ketones and is too mild for most esters. The selectivity is turned around.

choices.text: Both are reduced equally; NaBH4 shows no selectivity
choices.note: NaBH4 does tell them apart. The aldehyde reacts faster, which is exactly why one cold equivalent is used.

lockIt: Limited hydride, two carbonyls: the aldehyde reacts first because it is more positive and less crowded.
